label: Gaming / Interactive Entertainment
subject: {{domain}} — accessibility gaps your players (and lawyers) will notice
body:
Hi {{first_name}},

Ran an accessibility scan on {{domain}} and found {{total_issues}} WCAG 2.1 AA violations. The gaming industry is under a spotlight right now — Xbox, PlayStation, and Nintendo all shipped accessibility features in 2024-25, and the conversation has shifted from 'nice-to-have' to baseline expectation. Studios with inaccessible web properties are drawing the wrong kind of attention.

Three most urgent on {{business_name}}:

1. {{top_issue_1}} — game info pages, merch stores, and community portals with missing alt text or unlabeled interactive elements exclude the 15M+ gamers with disabilities in the US alone. That's a community that's vocal, loyal, and very aware of who does and doesn't care.

2. {{top_issue_2}} — navigation flows (store checkout, account management, event registration) that aren't keyboard-accessible create both legal exposure under ADA Title III and a PR risk. Accessibility advocacy groups in gaming have significant social reach.

3. {{top_issue_3}} — the ESA and industry groups have committed to accessibility standards. Studios without a web accessibility posture are falling behind their own industry's trajectory.

I can send {{business_name}} a free 17-point accessibility audit (with implementation-ready remediation code for your web team). No strings. If you want us to handle fixes: flat $1,200, 2 weeks.

Want to see the report?

— Emilio Ranucoli
